cat > .github/workflows/triage.yml <<'EOF'
---
name: triage

# pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository, so the token
# can write to pull requests opened from forks (plain `pull_request` gets a
# read-only token there). This is safe only because the workflow never checks
# out or executes code from the pull request.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Welcome and label
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      # Untrusted values are passed through env, never interpolated into the script.
      PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
      PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
    steps:
      - name: Ensure the needs-triage label exists
        run: gh label create needs-triage --description "Awaiting triage" --color FBCA04 || true

      - name: Apply the needs-triage label
        run: gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label needs-triage

      - name: Post the welcome comment
        run: |
          {
            printf 'Welcome, @%s! Thanks for your contribution.\n\n' "$PR_AUTHOR"
            printf 'Summary: **%s**\n\n' "$PR_TITLE"
            printf 'A maintainer will triage this pull request soon.\n'
          } > comment.md
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body-file comment.md
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Triage workflow

`.github/workflows/triage.yml` runs when a pull request is opened. It:

- posts a comment welcoming the author by username and repeating the pull request title as a summary;
- applies the `needs-triage` label (creating it if it does not exist).

It uses the `pull_request_target` trigger so the token can write comments and labels on pull requests opened from forks, where `pull_request` tokens are read-only. For that reason the workflow must never check out or run code from the pull request; it only calls the `gh` CLI, and the title and username are passed via environment variables rather than interpolated into shell code.
EOF

content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and a "Triage workflow" section in the README. I haven't run it, because it only fires on a real pull request opened on GitHub.

- **Trigger:** it runs when a pull request is opened.
- **Comment:** it posts "Welcome, @username!" followed by "Summary: **<PR title>**" and a note that a maintainer will triage soon.
- **Label:** it applies `needs-triage`, and creates the label first if the repo doesn't have it.
- **Forks:** the workflow uses `pull_request_target`, because the normal `pull_request` trigger gives forks a read-only token that can't comment or label. The workflow never checks out or runs the pull request's code, which is what makes `pull_request_target` safe here. Keep it that way if you edit it.
- **Untrusted input:** the title and username are passed in as environment variables, not interpolated into the shell script, so a crafted title can't inject commands.
- **Permissions:** the job gets only `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`. It uses the preinstalled `gh` CLI, so there are no third-party actions.

A title containing `@someone` will notify that person when the comment posts. I left that as is.
